title: India-EU Relations: Strategic and Economic Engagements

scenes.text: Why is the India-EU partnership called a loveless arranged marriage?
scenes.narration: Have you ever wondered why India and the European Union struggle to build a deep bond? Even though they became strategic partners in 2004, experts describe their relationship as a loveless arranged marriage.

scenes.text: Like two project partners who share notes but have different social circles.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy to understand this. Imagine two classmates assigned to work on a school project. You happily exchange textbooks for tests, but outside class, your social circles and interests never align.

scenes.heading: Milestones in India-EU Relations
scenes.narration: Look at how their journey unfolded. Formal ties began in the 1950s, leading to a partnership in 2004. In 2007, both sides launched Free Trade Agreement talks to eliminate tariffs and encourage investment.

scenes.heading: Diverging Geostrategic Priorities

columns.title: India
items: Pakistan and China are primary threats
Diverges on Crimea and Kashmir positions

scenes.narration: Here's the trick to understanding their foreign policy gap. The European Union views Russia as its primary security challenge, especially after Crimea was annexed. In contrast, India focuses on Pakistan and China, where European nations maintain cordial ties.

scenes.heading: Free Trade Agreement Sticking Points

columns.title: EU Demands
items: Tariff cuts on dairy and automobiles
Lower duties on wine and spirits
Stricter intellectual property rights in pharma

columns.title: India's Concerns
items: Wants liberalised movement for skilled professionals

scenes.narration: Notice why trade negotiations remain deadlocked. The EU wants lower tariffs on cars, wine, and dairy, but India protects three million dairy producers. Meanwhile, India demands data secure status for IT and easier movement for professionals.

scenes.heading: Why the EU Relationship Stalls
items: India prioritises bilateral ties with Germany and Britain
Bilateral success creates complacency on both sides
Lack of ownership in overall EU relations
EU distracted by domestic financial and Syrian crises
scenes.narration: Here is the structural problem. India maintains strong bilateral ties directly with Germany and Britain. Because these individual relationships prosper, both sides become complacent, leading to an absence of ownership in the broader EU partnership.

items: Strategic partnership lacks alignment on core security issues
Trade talks stall over agriculture, autos, and IT
Strong bilateral ties cause complacency and lack of ownership
scenes.narration: Remember these three big takeaways! First, strategic goals diverge sharply over Russia and China. Second, trade negotiations stall over agriculture, automobiles, and services. Finally, successful bilateral partnerships cause complacency, leaving the wider EU framework neglected.
